category_definition: Middle Eastern Grocery Store = a brick-and-mortar, walk-in retail storefront whose primary trade is groceries and specialty food from the Middle East / North Africa / South Asia diaspora, typically anchored by a halal (zabiha) meat counter and a staple line of rice, bulgur, lentils, dates, tahini, spices, breads and imported beverages. Subcategories observed in Milwaukee: (a) Arab/Levantine grocer-butcher (Samah, Amanah, Holy Land, Al-Yousef, Rayan, Jerusalem Market); (b) Persian market (Shirazi); (c) Indo-Pak / desi grocery (Raja Bazaar, Attari, Indian Bazaar, Maharaja, Janet Grocery, Zaika Mart); (d) East/Southeast African halal grocery (Garden of Eden, Kilimanjaro, Al-Ansar); (e) hybrid grocery + in-store kitchen/carryout (most of the above operate a shawarma/kebab/bakery counter). Business model is product-led retail with a hybrid prepared-food add-on; a minority are pure-butcher or bakery-led. Stores range from ~1,000 sq ft convenience-scale (Attari) to full supermarket scale (Holy Land).
geographic_classification_notes: Center of gravity is the South Side catchment: W Layton Ave / W Ramsey Ave / W Edgerton Ave (53221), S 13th St / Crisol corridor (53204-53221), W Historic Mitchell St (53204), W Lincoln Ave (53215), S 27th St (53221), and the S Howell Ave stretch in Oak Creek (53154). One North/East Side outlier (Shirazi, 2864 N Oakland, 53211) and one far Northwest outlier (Kilimanjaro, 6730 W Villard, 53218) break the south-side pattern. Adjacent-municipality findings cluster in Oak Creek (53154), Franklin (53132) and Brookfield (53005); the Brookfield cluster (Jerusalem Grocery & Deli, Zaika Mart, Raja Bazaar) sits along W Capitol Dr, outside the named corridor list. No qualifying storefront was found in the west-suburb ZIPs 53214/53227/53129/53130/53172 or the north-shore ZIPs 53217/53211 (other than Shirazi).
ownership_exclusion_notes: Excluded from the qualifying set: Walmart Supercenter (401 E Capitol Dr) as national_chain; Cermak Fresh Market (1277 S Barclay St) as regional_chain (multi-state IL/WI Cermak Family of Markets). Raja Bazaar is classified local_chain (2 metro locations: 709-711 W Mitchell, Milwaukee + 3065 N 124th St, Brookfield) and is retained — the two storefronts are recorded as separate candidates per the multi-location rule. No national_franchise was found in category. All other candidates are independent or unknown.

outreach_recommendation.platform_rationale: Google is where the gold standard is deepest for this category (Middle Eastern grocery store primary category, menu/order links, 100+ photo expectation) AND where this market's gap is widest: most qualifying storefronts have no claimed, correctly-categorized Business Profile at all — the community directories and hosted pages are doing the work Google should be doing. A correctly categorized, claimed, hours-complete Google profile is the single highest-leverage fixable gap.

platform_specific_opportunities.opportunity: At least 19 of 31 candidates have no resolvable claimed GBP; several that do (Al-Yousef, Rayan, Garden of Eden) carry a restaurant-leaning or generic category instead of a grocery category.
platform_specific_opportunities.evidence_summary: Only ~12 candidates show any Google presence; misaligned categories observed for Attari, Al-Yousef, Garden of Eden, Shirazi, Maharaja.

platform_specific_opportunities.opportunity: Yelp coverage is near-empty and actively misleading: Attari — a genuine grocery-butcher — is filed under 'Bakeries'. 27 of 31 candidates have no Yelp page found.
platform_specific_opportunities.evidence_summary: 4 Yelp presences located; Cermak unclaimed; most storefronts absent entirely.

platform_specific_opportunities.opportunity: Facebook is the de-facto operating surface for several stores (Attari ~692 followers) yet most storefronts have no page, losing the local-referral channel this category actually uses.
platform_specific_opportunities.evidence_summary: 5 Facebook presences located; community referrals happen in FB groups with no owned page behind them.

platform_specific_opportunities.opportunity: Apple Maps place cards are largely unclaimed; Apple Business Connect is an unclaimed, low-cost photo/showcase channel for the S 27th St and Layton Ave clusters.
platform_specific_opportunities.evidence_summary: Only Jerusalem Market shows a clean 'International Grocery Store' card; others unverified.

outreach_recommendation.primary_angle: These are real, community-trusted halal grocers that a walk-in customer can find by driving past — but a customer searching 'Middle Eastern grocery near me' often cannot find them, because their Google presence is missing, unclaimed, or filed under the wrong category. The opportunity is discovery repair, not reputation repair: claim the profile, set the correct grocery category, publish hours, and let the existing community trust do the rest.
outreach_recommendation.suggested_call_to_action: Claim and correctly categorize your Google Business Profile — a short, guided setup that puts your store in front of customers already searching for halal and Middle Eastern groceries in Milwaukee.
